source.name: ONCHigh
source.citation: Phansalkar S, Desai AA, Bell D, et al. High-priority drug-drug interactions for use in electronic health records. J Am Med Inform Assoc. 2012;19(5):735-743. doi:10.1136/amiajnl-2011-000612

deferred_rules.reason: Open-ended class requires an authoritative QT-prolonger list (CredibleMeds QTdrugs); ingested as a separate source.

rules.mechanism: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors block catecholamine metabolism, while amphetamine-type stimulants and related indirect sympathomimetics release catecholamines; concurrent exposure elevates synaptic norepinephrine and dopamine and can precipitate hypertensive crisis.
rules.management: Stimulant prescribing information labels concurrent MAOI use as contraindicated and specifies a 14-day washout after MAOI discontinuation before initiating the stimulant.

rules.mechanism: Atazanavir dissolution requires an acidic gastric environment; proton pump inhibitors elevate gastric pH, substantially reducing atazanavir absorption and plasma concentrations with risk of sub-therapeutic antiretroviral exposure and virologic failure.
rules.management: Atazanavir prescribing information labels concomitant PPI use as not recommended in treatment-experienced patients and contraindicated in PPI-naive patients; when use is unavoidable, PPI dose is limited and dosing is separated in time with ritonavir boosting.

rules.mechanism: Febuxostat inhibits xanthine oxidase, which normally inactivates the active metabolites of azathioprine and mercaptopurine; coadministration can increase thiopurine exposure and produce severe myelosuppression.
rules.management: Febuxostat prescribing information labels concurrent azathioprine or mercaptopurine use as contraindicated.

rules.mechanism: Serotonergic antidepressants elevate synaptic serotonin; concurrent monoamine oxidase inhibition compounds serotonergic activity and can precipitate serotonin syndrome.
rules.management: Serotonergic antidepressant prescribing information labels concurrent MAOI use as contraindicated and specifies a 14-day washout in each direction; fluoxetine requires a 5-week washout before initiating an MAOI owing to the long half-life of norfluoxetine.

rules.mechanism: Irinotecan is activated to SN-38 and subsequently glucuronidated by UGT1A1; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can elevate irinotecan and SN-38 plasma exposure, increasing risk of severe neutropenia and diarrhea.
rules.management: Irinotecan prescribing information labels avoidance of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors during treatment or, when unavoidable, dose reduction with close monitoring for myelosuppression and gastrointestinal toxicity.

rules.object_class: Opioid and opioid-like analgesics with serotonergic activity
rules.mechanism: Meperidine, tramadol, tapentadol, methadone, fentanyl, and dextromethorphan have serotonergic activity; concurrent monoamine oxidase inhibition can precipitate serotonin syndrome, with additional risk of hypertensive crisis reported historically with meperidine.
rules.management: Labels for meperidine, tramadol, tapentadol, fentanyl, methadone, and dextromethorphan-containing products specify contraindication with MAOIs and a 14-day washout in each direction.

rules.mechanism: Tricyclic antidepressants inhibit serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake; concurrent monoamine oxidase inhibition compounds monoaminergic activity and can precipitate hypertensive crisis and serotonin syndrome.
rules.management: Tricyclic antidepressant prescribing information labels concurrent MAOI use as contraindicated and specifies a 14-day washout in each direction.

rules.mechanism: Ramelteon is metabolized primarily by CYP1A2; coadministration with fluvoxamine has been reported to increase ramelteon AUC approximately 190-fold.
rules.management: Ramelteon prescribing information labels concurrent fluvoxamine use as contraindicated and advises caution with other strong CYP1A2 inhibitors.

rules.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducers accelerate protease inhibitor metabolism, reducing antiretroviral plasma exposure and risking virologic failure and resistance.
rules.management: Protease inhibitor prescribing information advises against coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers such as rifampin, rifapentine, and St John's wort; alternative therapy or, for some combinations, dose adjustment with rifabutin is specified.

rules.mechanism: Simvastatin and lovastatin are extensively metabolized by CYP3A4; strong inhibitors elevate statin plasma exposure and risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
rules.management: Simvastatin and lovastatin prescribing information labels concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (including HIV protease inhibitors, clarithromycin, telithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone, cobicistat) as contraindicated.

rules.mechanism: Ergot alkaloid metabolism is CYP3A4-dependent; concurrent strong inhibition elevates ergot exposure with risk of ergotism, peripheral vasospasm, and tissue ischemia.
rules.management: Ergotamine and dihydroergotamine prescribing information labels concurrent use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (HIV protease inhibitors, macrolide antibiotics, and azole antifungals) as contraindicated.

rules.mechanism: Tizanidine is metabolized primarily by CYP1A2; concurrent CYP1A2 inhibitors markedly increase tizanidine plasma exposure with risk of severe hypotension and sedation.
rules.management: Tizanidine prescribing information labels concurrent use with fluvoxamine or ciprofloxacin as contraindicated and advises avoidance of other CYP1A2 inhibitors.

rules.mechanism: Both agents inhibit monoamine oxidase; concurrent exposure amplifies catecholamine- and serotonin-mediated effects and can precipitate hypertensive crisis and serotonin syndrome.
rules.management: Concurrent use of two monoamine oxidase inhibitors is contraindicated per prescribing information; a 14-day washout between agents is specified.

rules.mechanism: Sumatriptan, zolmitriptan, and rizatriptan are partially metabolized by monoamine oxidase type A; concurrent MAOI use elevates triptan exposure and compounds serotonergic activity, with risk of serotonin syndrome.
rules.management: Prescribing information for MAO-A metabolized triptans labels concurrent MAOI use as contraindicated and specifies a 2-week washout in each direction.
